facts.fact: The page states that U.S. advertisers are expected to spend $130.97 billion on video advertising by 2025.
facts.quote: By 2025, it’s expected that U.S. advertisers will pour **$130.97 billion** into video advertising.

facts.fact: The page reports that U.S. video advertising spend was $111.55 billion in 2024.
facts.quote: That’s a huge leap from $111.55 billion in 2024

facts.fact: The page advises that in-stream video ads have about 3-5 seconds to earn viewer attention.
facts.quote: You have about **3-5** seconds to earn their attention.

facts.fact: The page defines in-stream advertising as any video ad that plays inside a video player right before, during, or after the content the viewer came to see.
facts.quote: At its core, **in-stream advertising** is any video ad that plays inside a video player, right before, during, or after the content you came to see.

facts.fact: The page identifies three in-stream ad placements: pre-roll (before the video), mid-roll (during the video), and post-roll (after the video).
facts.quote: These ads typically show up in one of three spots:

facts.fact: The page's bakery example describes a 15-second video ad shot for a pre-roll campaign.
facts.quote: They shot a quick, 15-second video that was pure food-lover bait

facts.fact: The page's bakery example used geo-targeting to show its ad only to people within a five-mile radius of the shop.
facts.quote: They used geo-targeting to show their ad only to people in a five-mile radius of the shop.

facts.fact: The page's bakery example reported a 25% increase in weekday morning foot traffic after its ad campaign.
facts.quote: They saw a **25% bump** in weekday morning foot traffic

facts.fact: The page's bakery example offered a free coffee with any pastry, valid Monday through Thursday before 10 AM.
facts.quote: Mention this ad for a free coffee with any pastry, Monday through Thursday before 10 AM.

facts.fact: The page's B2B tech startup example used a 60-second mid-roll ad in the form of a mini-tutorial.
facts.quote: It was a 60-second "mini-tutorial" that showed off a unique feature solving a very specific problem

facts.fact: The page's B2B tech startup example reported a 40% increase in qualified leads in one quarter.
facts.quote: They saw a **40% increase in qualified leads** in just one quarter

facts.fact: The page states that 54% of streaming video subscribers now use at least one ad-supported tier, a large increase from the previous year; the page links to Nielsen.com for trend data but does not explicitly attribute this figure to Nielsen.
facts.quote: In fact, **54%** of streaming video subscribers now use at least one ad-supported tier

facts.fact: The page states that streaming makes up nearly 44% of all TV time in the U.S.; the page links to Nielsen.com for related trends but does not explicitly attribute this figure to Nielsen.
facts.quote: with streaming now making up nearly **44%** of all TV time in the U.S.

facts.fact: The page defines view-through rate (VTR) as the percentage of people shown an ad who watched it all the way through or for a significant portion of it.
facts.quote: This simply tells you what percentage of people who were shown your ad watched it all the way through

facts.fact: The page defines click-through rate (CTR) as the percentage of viewers who were compelled enough by an ad to click on it.
facts.quote: This is the percentage of viewers who were compelled enough by your ad to click on it.

facts.fact: The page states that the average click-through rate for in-stream ads hovers around 0.90%.
facts.quote: The average click-through rate (CTR) for in-stream ads hovers around 0.90%.

facts.fact: The page states that in-stream ad click-through rates in retail can reach about 1.59%.
facts.quote: in more visual fields like retail, it can jump to 1.59%

facts.fact: The page says Adwave creates ads and manages their placement on TV, search, and social, and that users can review the campaign before launch.
facts.quote: Adwave creates ads and manages their placement on TV, search, and social. You can review the campaign before launch.
